original_finding.first_contract: AnimationSampleRate admits a finite positive hertz value when its f32 reciprocal is a positive finite duration. PoseBufferConfig separately admits a positive minimum bake duration and its displayed validation does not bound their product. bake_clip checks that duration/interval is finite and fits usize, then samples every frame into three vectors for every joint; representability is not a practical work or memory bound.
original_finding.condition: For example, a validated configuration can contain pose sample_hz 1e9 and a minimum grid duration of 1 second, giving on the order of one billion samples per channel per joint while remaining below the usize representability check on ordinary 32-/64-bit targets. A successfully loaded finite-duration clip with at least one joint must reach baking, and platform/resource behavior is not observed. No configuration, fixture, product or runtime probe was executed.
original_finding.future_direction: Define an accepted frame/channel/joint work budget at the clip-bake owner before allocation, or reject excessively large sampling configurations with structured context. Preserve ordinary frame endpoints, duration rounding and existing native error behavior.
relationships: Related to 059 Q-L1-aad423b852c6981cae42 on baked-grid admission and broader sample-rate/current producer obligations, but a resource budget is a separate condition from nonfinite/usize overflow; root determines exact repair identity. No alias inferred solely from another unbounded geometric-work issue.

original_finding.first_contract: ReferenceAcceleration admits any finite strictly positive f32, and body target divides an acceleration component by it before multiplying by an authored angle. A sufficiently small positive reference and finite acceleration can produce a nonfinite ratio/product; BodyAngle admission rejects it before the subsequent clamp.
original_finding.condition: A validated installed tuning with the relevant small reference and positive/nonzero angle, a finite input acceleration reaching the body-response branch, and intended support for that extreme domain are needed. A mathematical example is reference 1e-40 and acceleration 1, without claiming such tuning was installed or gameplay observed. The ordinary shipped reference values are not inferred to fail.
original_finding.future_direction: Clarify supported authored reference/acceleration domain and prevent or explicitly classify overflow at the owning numerical operation while preserving intended clamp, finite error and normal response behavior.

original_finding.first_contract: AnimationSampleSpan stores a u64 and duration conversion deliberately casts the sample count to f32 before division by hertz, then re-admits elapsed time. Distinct large counts can therefore round to the same f32, and sufficiently large spans at sufficiently low valid sample rates can yield a nonfinite duration and return an error. The displayed AttackFacing caller propagates that error.
original_finding.condition: The actual supported range of active deadline spans, sample rates and failure policy is not established; this source behavior alone does not demonstrate a product failure. Zero spans remain valid and reciprocal construction is checked.
original_finding.future_direction: Establish supported clock and deadline domains, then decide whether to retain the documented f32 count-before-division behavior, bound inputs, or use a more precise domain at the authoritative time conversion while preserving intended errors and zero semantics.
relationships: 059 Adler READ-L11-260 already preserved count-before-division and left large-span/low-rate caller behavior open; this bounded current consumer connection does not promote that historical read or close the queue.
